segments.text: Greetings! Welcome, friends.
segments.englishExplanation: A friendly greeting welcoming visitors.

segments.text: I'll be right down.
segments.englishExplanation: The speaker says they are coming downstairs immediately.

segments.text: Could I interest you in some peppermint tea?
segments.englishExplanation: A polite offer asking if the guests would like to have some peppermint tea.
segments.turkishExplanation: Biraz nane çayı ikram etsem içer misiniz?

segments.text: What are you guys? We are sprites.
segments.englishExplanation: A question asking what kind of beings they are, followed by their answer identifying themselves as sprites.

segments.text: We sprite balance to the forest.
segments.englishExplanation: A playful statement asserting that they maintain balance in the forest.

segments.text: We take care of the animals.
segments.englishExplanation: The speaker explains that their duty includes looking after the forest animals.

learningPoints.englishExplanation: A courteous, hospitable way to offer someone food, drink, or an idea.
learningPoints.turkishExplanation: Birine kibarca bir yiyecek, içecek veya fikir teklif etmek ya da ikramda bulunmak için kullanılan nazik bir kalıptır.
learningPoints.exampleEn: Could I interest you in a slice of homemade cake?
learningPoints.exampleTr: Ev yapımı bir dilim kek ikram etsem yer misiniz?

learningPoints.englishExplanation: A common phrasal verb meaning to look after, protect, or attend to the needs of someone or something.
learningPoints.turkishExplanation: Birine veya bir şeye bakmak, onunla ilgilenmek ya da onun sorumluluğunu üstlenmek anlamına gelen yaygın bir deyimsel fiildir.
learningPoints.exampleEn: Don't worry about the plants; I'll take care of them while you're away.
learningPoints.exampleTr: Bitkiler için endişelenme; sen yokken onlarla ben ilgilenirim.

quiz.question: In the video, what does the speaker mean by "Could I interest you in some peppermint tea?"

options.text: Would you like me to serve you some peppermint tea?
Do you know how to prepare fresh peppermint tea?
Are you willing to buy some peppermint tea from me?
Why do you prefer peppermint tea over other drinks?

issues.message: Learning point ifadesi ("Could I interest you in...?") segment 3'in transcript metninde literal olarak bulunamadı — pedagojik notation/çekim farkı olabilir, yanlış pozitif olasılığı var.

attribution.title: Sprite Fright
attribution.changes: Filmden kısa kesit seçimi ve H.264/AAC kodlama yapıldı; orijinal İngilizce diyalog, müzik ve efektler değiştirilmeden korundu.

segments.text: Hey, uh,
segments.englishExplanation: A casual hesitation before addressing someone.

segments.text: little mushroom geezer, you call with us camping here for the night? Absolutely.
segments.englishExplanation: Asking the small mushroom character if it is alright to camp there overnight, and receiving an enthusiastic yes.
segments.turkishExplanation: Küçük mantar ihtiyar, bu gece burada kamp yapmamız senin için uygun mu? Kesinlikle.

segments.text: A friend of the forest is a friend of the sprites.
segments.englishExplanation: A rhyming proverb expressing that anyone kind to nature is welcome among woodland spirits.

segments.text: Maybe, maybe it was just ketchup or something like red paint?
segments.englishExplanation: Speculating nervously that a suspicious red substance was merely harmless sauce or paint.
segments.turkishExplanation: Belki de, belki sadece ketçap ya da kırmızı boya gibi bir şeydi?

segments.text: Yeah, maybe they were just painting their little hats or something. Mmm. Brrr.
segments.englishExplanation: Agreeing with the hopeful excuse while shivering with unease.
segments.turkishExplanation: Evet, belki de sadece küçük şapkalarını falan boyuyorlardı. Hım. Brrr.

learningPoints.englishExplanation: Used to describe staying or doing something during the overnight period until the next morning.
learningPoints.turkishExplanation: Gece boyunca kalmayı ya da bir yerde gecelemeyi ifade eden kalıp.
learningPoints.exampleEn: Can we stay at your place for the night?

quiz.question: In the video, what does the saying "A friend of the forest is a friend of the sprites" mean?

options.text: Anyone who respects the woods is welcomed by the magical creatures living there.
Only magical creatures are permitted to enter and spend the night in the forest.
Campers must bring gifts to the spirits if they want to stay safe until morning.
Forest spirits distrust any strangers who try to build a campsite nearby.

attribution.title: Sprite Fright
attribution.changes: Filmden kısa kesit seçimi ve H.264/AAC kodlama yapıldı; orijinal İngilizce diyalog, müzik ve efektler değiştirilmeden korundu.

segments.text: They're absolutely adorable!
segments.englishExplanation: The speaker expresses delight at how extremely cute the creatures are.

segments.text: Yeah, absolutely bloody adorable!
segments.englishExplanation: The speaker strongly agrees, using informal emphasis to describe their cuteness.

segments.text: And I bet we'll make a fortune if we catch one of those things.
segments.englishExplanation: The speaker predicts that catching one of the creatures will bring them a huge amount of money.
segments.turkishExplanation: Ve bahse girerim o şeylerden birini yakalarsak köşeyi döneriz.

segments.text: We'll be famous! Get on MTV!
segments.englishExplanation: The speaker excitedly imagines becoming celebrities and appearing on music television.

segments.text: I wonder what they taste like.
segments.englishExplanation: The speaker wonders aloud what the creatures would taste like if eaten.

segments.text: Oh, we really shouldn't disrupt their habitat.
segments.englishExplanation: The speaker brings up the concern that they should avoid disturbing the creatures' natural living space.

segments.text: Right, sure, sure. Greetings!
segments.englishExplanation: The speaker quickly agrees and greets the creatures.

learningPoints.englishExplanation: An idiom meaning to earn or acquire a very large amount of money.
learningPoints.turkishExplanation: Çok büyük miktarda para kazanmak veya zengin olmak anlamına gelen yaygın bir deyim.
learningPoints.exampleEn: He made a fortune investing in real estate at a young age.
learningPoints.exampleTr: Genç yaşta gayrimenkule yatırım yaparak köşeyi döndü.

quiz.question: In segment 3, what does the speaker mean by the phrase "make a fortune"?

options.text: Earn a very large amount of money
Have good luck and avoid danger
Become respected wild animal experts
Build a successful outdoor business

attribution.title: Sprite Fright
attribution.changes: Filmden kısa kesit seçimi ve H.264/AAC kodlama yapıldı; orijinal İngilizce diyalog, müzik ve efektler değiştirilmeden korundu.

segments.text: Hello, Mr Snail!
segments.englishExplanation: A friendly greeting addressed to a snail.

segments.text: Oh, you cute little corny wassparsum!
segments.englishExplanation: An affectionate and playful remark calling the creature a silly, cute nickname.
segments.turkishExplanation: Ayy, seni sevimli küçük şapşal şey!

segments.text: That name is bonus points!
segments.englishExplanation: Suggests that the invented name deserves special recognition or extra praise.

segments.text: Ugh, can't believe we got stuck with a tree hugger!
segments.englishExplanation: An expression of frustration at having to spend time with someone overly obsessed with nature.
segments.turkishExplanation: Öf, başımıza bir doğa aşığı kaldığına inanamıyorum!

learningPoints.englishExplanation: An informal idiom meaning to be forced to spend time with someone or deal with an unpleasant task that nobody else wants.
learningPoints.turkishExplanation: İstenmeyen bir durumla baş başa kalmak veya hoşlanılmayan birine mecburen katlanmak zorunda kalındığında 'başına kalmak' anlamında kullanılır.
learningPoints.exampleEn: Everyone went home, and I got stuck with all the dirty dishes.
learningPoints.exampleTr: Herkes eve gitti ve bütün bulaşıklar benim başıma kaldı.

learningPoints.englishExplanation: An informal, often teasing or mildly derogatory label for someone who is enthusiastic about nature and environmental conservation.
learningPoints.turkishExplanation: Çevreyi, ağaçları ve hayvanları korumaya aşırı önem veren kişilere genellikle hafif alaycı veya sitemkar bir tonla verilen lakap.
learningPoints.exampleEn: Stop being such a tree hugger; it's just a tiny bug!
learningPoints.exampleTr: Bu kadar doğa delisi olma; alt tarafı küçücük bir böcek!

quiz.question: In the video, what does the speaker imply by saying they 'got stuck with a tree hugger'?

options.text: They are annoyed to be paired with someone overly sentimental about nature.
They are physically trapped in the woods with an outdoor enthusiast.
They are grateful to have found someone who cares about animals.
They were penalized for not knowing enough about local wildlife.

attribution.title: Sprite Fright
attribution.changes: Filmden kısa kesit seçimi ve H.264/AAC kodlama yapıldı; orijinal İngilizce diyalog, müzik ve efektler değiştirilmeden korundu.

segments.text: Way ahead of you, man. Come on, team.
segments.englishExplanation: Saying you have already anticipated what someone is suggesting, and encouraging the group to move.
segments.turkishExplanation: Ben o işi çoktan hallettim dostum. Hadi takım, toparlanın.

segments.text: We must have dilly -dally when there's so much nature to see.
segments.englishExplanation: Urging not to waste time or loiter because there is a lot of nature to explore.
segments.turkishExplanation: Görülecek bunca doğa varken öyle boş boş oyalanmak olmaz.

segments.text: I was thinking we should call our class project fun guys in a forest. Get it?
segments.englishExplanation: Suggesting a pun-based name for the group assignment and checking if the listener caught the joke.
segments.turkishExplanation: Dönem ödevimizin adını 'Ormandaki Eğlenceli Tipler' koysak diyordum. Çaktınız mı espriyi?

segments.text: Because we're a group of fun guys and also fun guys. Shush!
segments.englishExplanation: Explaining the double meaning between 'fun guys' and 'fungi' before being silenced.
segments.turkishExplanation: Çünkü hem eğlenceli çocuklarız hem de birer mantarız! Şşş, sessiz ol!

segments.text: That's the low bar team.
segments.englishExplanation: Commenting that the joke sets an extremely low standard for humor.

segments.text: And she's in distress.
segments.englishExplanation: Observing that a female is currently in trouble or in need of rescue.

learningPoints.englishExplanation: Used colloquially to tell someone that you have already done, thought of, or prepared what they are about to suggest.
learningPoints.turkishExplanation: Birinin önereceği şeyi zaten çoktan düşündüğünüzü, planladığınızı veya yaptığınızı belirtmek için kullanılan samimi bir kalıptır.
learningPoints.exampleEn: Don't forget to lock the back door. — Way ahead of you, I already did.
learningPoints.exampleTr: Arka kapıyı kilitlemeyi unutma. — Benden önce davrandın sanma, çoktan kilitledim bile.

learningPoints.englishExplanation: Refers to a very low standard, expectation, or level of quality that is extremely easy to reach or disappointingly poor.
learningPoints.turkishExplanation: Beklentinin veya kalite standardının çok düşük tutulduğunu anlatan mecazi bir ifadedir ('çıtanın düşük olması').
learningPoints.exampleEn: If remembering my birthday makes him a great friend, that's a pretty low bar.
learningPoints.exampleTr: Doğum günümü hatırlaması onu harika bir dost yapıyorsa, çıta gerçekten epey düşük demektir.

quiz.question: In segment 5, what does the speaker mean by describing the joke as 'the low bar'?

options.text: It relies on a very poor standard of humor.
It presents a physical obstacle in the forest.
It sets a goal that is nearly impossible to meet.
It violates the formal rules of the school project.

issues.message: "dilly-dally" transcript metninde literal olarak bulunamadı — çekim/inflection farkı olabilir, yanlış pozitif olasılığı var.
